title: ABNT NBR ISO/CIE 8995-1:2013; ISO/CIE 8995-1:2025; AMEV guidance on DIN EN 12464-1 classroom lighting; DIAL school lighting summary; Vishay VEML7700 documentation; and peer-reviewed studies on one-point classroom daylight measurement and low-cost lux-sensor performance
author_or_body: ABNT; ISO/TC 274 and CIE; Arbeitskreis Maschinen- und Elektrotechnik staatlicher und kommunaler Verwaltungen (AMEV); DIAL; Vishay Semiconductors; Suarez-Garcia et al.; Ackley, Donn, and Thomas
edition_year: ABNT NBR ISO/CIE 8995-1 published 2013-03-21; ISO/CIE 8995-1 published 2025-01; AMEV recommendation page published 2025; DIAL knowledge-base summary updated 2016; VEML7700 product information current as indexed in 2026; peer-reviewed supporting papers from 2018 and 2022
source_type: Standards-backed synthesis combining a Brazilian national standard catalog/status entry, international standard status pages, an official public DIN EN 12464-1 summary, a standards-derived school-lighting summary, manufacturer documentation, and peer-reviewed primary studies.
normative_status: ABNT NBR ISO/CIE 8995-1:2013 is publicly sold as a current Brazilian standard, while ISO 8995-1:2002 was withdrawn and replaced internationally by ISO/CIE 8995-1:2025 on 2025-01-31; whether Brazil has already published an ABNT adoption aligned to the 2025 international revision is [uncertain].
source_hierarchy: Highest weight: Brazil-specific standard status and indexed excerpts for ABNT NBR ISO/CIE 8995-1:2013 because the case study is in Brazil. Next: ISO/CIE 8995-1:2025 and the AMEV DIN EN 12464-1 summary for current international and European status/context. Then: Vishay documentation for VEML7700 metrology and peer-reviewed papers for the limits of one-point classroom illuminance measurement.
country_or_jurisdiction: Brazil first, supplemented by international and German/European references where the latest Brazilian adoption path after ISO/CIE 8995-1:2025 is [uncertain].
environment_type: Occupied indoor classrooms used at night, with electric lighting as the main source and possible residual daylight near dusk; also relevant to board or blackboard viewing surfaces inside the same room.
occupant_profile: Adult learners and teachers, with corrected-to-normal visual tasks such as reading, writing, board viewing, and note taking.
room_operation_mode: Most applicable to mechanically lit classrooms, and still usable in mixed-mode classrooms where daylight, blinds, and projector scenes may change local conditions; the exact room mode in the case study is [uncertain].
operating_context: Interpret readings during occupied night classes, documenting whether luminaires are on, dimmed, failed, or intentionally reduced for projection, and whether windows, blinds, or strong daylight gradients are still affecting the room near the start of the evening period. The exact operating pattern of the selected room is [uncertain].
excluded_conditions: Do not transfer these values directly to art rooms, technical drawing rooms, laboratories, sports spaces, projector-only darkened scenes, or daylight-only design simulations without checking the relevant activity-specific requirement. A single-point VEML7700 reading also does not replace a formal room-wide compliance survey.
limit_or_range: For the Brazil-specific adult-education interpretation used here, maintain about 500 lx on the classroom working plane and about 500 lx vertical on the board or blackboard, with planned uniformity of at least Uo 0.60 on the classroom work area and at least Uo 0.70 on the board. A current German/European public summary also states that newer DIN EN 12464-1 practice treats classrooms generally at 500 lx, but the directly applicable Brazilian post-2025 adoption status is [uncertain].
meaning_of_parameter: This is a lighting adequacy and maintenance parameter for visual task performance, visual comfort support, and lighting-system screening. In the dashboard context it should be used as a technical screening indicator, not as a full statement about comfort, pedagogy, or legal compliance.
spatial_reference_zone: For flexible or unknown desk layout, treat essentially the whole classroom as the task area while ignoring a marginal strip of about 0.5 m near the perimeter, and evaluate the work plane plus the board or blackboard separately. A local node reading represents only its own point unless a grid survey demonstrates broader equivalence.
measurement_position: For work-plane assessment, use a horizontal reference plane around 0.75 m above the floor and keep the sensor away from direct sun patches, window edges, board luminaires, projector beams, and enclosure self-shadowing. For board checks, measure the vertical writing area on the board surface itself. If a proxy wall point is used instead of desk-plane placement, document that it is a proxy rather than a compliance point.
sensor_orientation: Level and upward-facing for horizontal work-plane illuminance; normal to the board surface for board illuminance; if using a wall-mounted proxy point, keep the sensing face vertical and record that orientation explicitly.
spatial_representativeness: A single VEML7700 provides only point illuminance. It may track a local condition or, in some room geometries, approximate center-plane trends, but it cannot prove room-wide uniformity, board compliance, or daylight distribution over time. Formal compliance requires multiple points or an area/grid method, not one point.
unmeasured_relevant_variables: Glare, luminance distribution, reflections on the board, wall and ceiling brightness, vertical eye illuminance, spectral quality, color rendering, blind position, projector use, task variation, seating distribution, and daylight autonomy remain outside a single-point lux reading.
instrument_specification: VEML7700 digital ambient-light sensor with I2C interface. Recent Vishay selector material lists roughly 0 to 140000 lx and 0.0042 lx resolution, while older datasheet mirrors list about 0 to 167000 lx and 0.005 lx. Public manufacturer material indicates spectral shaping toward the human photopic response and published angular sensitivity behavior, but revision-to-revision numeric details differ [uncertain].
calibration_status: An assembled VEML7700 node is not automatically a calibrated compliance lux meter. Before using it for anything beyond rough screening, compare the installed sensor against a calibrated reference lux meter in the same orientation, mounting position, enclosure window, and lighting scenes expected in the room.
response_time: Selectable integration times of about 25, 50, 100, 200, 400, and 800 ms are commonly documented for VEML7700 implementations; longer integration improves low-light stability and shorter integration responds faster to scene changes.
sensor_hysteresis_and_drift: No strong classroom-specific public drift or hysteresis figure was found in the source set. Treat dust on the optical path, cover-glass attenuation, temperature bias from nearby electronics, and long-term fouling as the practical stability risks, and assume remaining drift behavior is [uncertain].
sampling_interval: For classroom dashboards, a raw sample interval around 10 s to 60 s is a practical engineering choice, followed by short aggregation for display and alerts [uncertain].
valid_data_requirement: Use only windows with enough non-saturated, non-missing samples to characterize the period; a practical rule such as at least 80% valid samples in the aggregation window is an engineering choice rather than a normative lighting requirement [uncertain].
gap_and_outlier_handling: Flag missing, saturated, implausibly flat, or abruptly shifted readings; suppress alerts during startup, sensor relocation, or known projector scenes; and retain raw data for audit. The exact thresholds for outliers and gap filling are engineering choices [uncertain].
aggregation_window: A short occupied-period aggregation such as a 1 min median or mean is suitable for dashboard readability, but the exact window is a project engineering decision [uncertain].
trigger_rule: For a local screening alert, trigger when the occupied aggregated point value remains below the chosen adult-education target for a sustained period such as 10 min to 15 min. This should be labeled as a point-based screening rule, not proof that the whole room fails the standard [uncertain].
clear_rule: Clear the point-based alert only after the aggregated value returns above the threshold for a sustained period, optionally with a small hysteresis buffer such as +50 lx to prevent oscillation; exact timing and hysteresis are engineering choices [uncertain].
rule_basis: Illuminance and uniformity targets come from standards-derived classroom lighting requirements, while persistence, aggregation, hysteresis, and rearm behavior are project engineering rules because no normative alert-timing rule was found.
dashboard_message: Example message: 'Point illuminance at the sensor location stayed below the adult-education target during the recent occupied window; this indicates a local lighting shortfall or local measurement condition and does not by itself prove whole-room non-compliance.' [uncertain]
possible_management_investigation: Check whether the classroom lights were switched on, dimmed, failed, shaded, blocked, or intentionally reduced for projection; verify sensor orientation, cleanliness, shadows, and distance from windows or luminaires; and compare the sensor point with the actual seated task area and the board area.
interpretation_limits: Do not infer full visual comfort, glare control, student performance, or legal compliance from one VEML7700 point. A point lux value cannot establish room-wide uniformity, board legibility, wall or ceiling brightness, or whether discomfort glare and reflections are controlled.
overinterpretation_risk: The largest risk is treating one lux value as if it represented the entire classroom. In classrooms with strong daylight gradients, flexible seating, or dedicated board lighting, a single point can be materially higher or lower than the rest of the room and still appear numerically plausible.
project_requirement: Provide technically grounded illuminance parameters for the TCC dashboard and alert logic while making explicit that the node supports local screening and trend monitoring rather than formal room-wide lighting certification.
destination_in_text: Use in the TCC methods section for sensor placement and orientation, in the alert-rule section for threshold justification, and in the limitations/discussion section for point-measurement representativeness and VEML7700 metrology caveats.
verification_state: Partially verified in original or official pages for standard status and sensor documentation, and in public standards summaries and peer-reviewed papers for classroom values and one-point-measurement limits. The exact Brazilian adoption path after ISO/CIE 8995-1:2025 remains [uncertain].
